analysis.title: Liar Liar Leather Jacket On Fire
key_insights: Hedge funds cut risk aggressively last week, but net deleveraging is less severe than during the Iran-war selloff. Gross leverage ratios rose because fund equity fell faster than gross exposure.
GS Prime: Info Tech was by far the most dollar net sold global and US sector. The week's percentage selling in global tech was about on par with the largest net selling weeks on record (since 2016).
GS Prime: the trailing 20-day pace of hedge fund selling in global AI stocks is the largest in more than five years (-3.0 SDs vs 5-year).
GS trading desk: hedge fund exposure to semis is now single digit.
Mag7 net length remains high at the 87th percentile over 1 year and the 93rd percentile over 3 years. The group had one of its biggest down moves in several years on Thursday.
Nasdaq 100 forward P/E fell to 18.4x, below its five- and ten-year averages and the lowest since 2020 (FactSet).
GS trading desk: top-of-book E-mini liquidity dropped as dealers pulled back during the selloff.

GS buyback desk: S&P buyback demand is running at about $5bn a day and 90% of corporates are in the open window Monday. Program trading volumes this week are about 1.4x 2025 YTD ADTV vs 0.6x the prior week.
Allegations about Jensen Huang are circulating over the weekend and are unverified. NVDA is barely up YTD and RSI is at levels last seen during Liberation Day (Bloomberg).
The Market Ear notes Berkshire has outperformed Nvidia by roughly 15 percentage points over the past year.

sector_views.rationale: Record-pace hedge fund selling and a forward P/E at a multi-year low point to a washed-out setup, but Mag7 positioning is still long and liquidity is thin.

risk_factors: Unverified allegations about Jensen Huang could hit sentiment on NVDA.
Mag7 positioning remains crowded long despite the selloff.
Hedge fund selling in tech and AI could continue.
